messages:
Marta: Quick sync — we need to firm the alpha slate for the Optimize toolkit (batching / caching / quantization recs + eval-triggered alerts). Customer asks from LibraryCo trial + Stripe pilot + Platform SRE. Can everyone drop must-haves and risks by EOD Friday?
Jia: Engineering must-haves: short list — 1) batching heuristics for mobile short-turn prompts (max latency bump <=25ms), 2) a lightweight prefix/KV cache API for session reuse, 3) quant profiles (int8 and int4 fallbacks) with smoke-level quality checks, 4) eval-triggered alert endpoint (webhook) + basic dashboard events.
Owen: For launch gating we need acceptance metrics: cost delta target >= 8-12% for typical workloads, quality regression <1% measured by NIST-style evals for top 50 prompts, tail latency 99p stays within SLO. If any of those fail we roll back.
Priya: Customer asks (LibraryCo/Stripe): - one-click apply of recommended profile per environment, - per-customer opt-out for auto-quantize, - telemetry exposed to customers (tokens saved, avg latency). LibraryCo specifically wants deterministic recommendations for chat-heavy sessions.
Kai: Infra notes: telemetry requires minor changes to trace schema (add recommend_reason field). Rollout flags for per-customer opt-in; we'll need a canary path in Dedicated so we don't impact hosted customers. Also need a quick explainer for KMS handling on Private.
Marta: Good. Proposed MVP (alpha): 1) Recommendation engine that suggests batching profile + cache policy + quant profile, 2) One-click apply in Console (basic rollback), 3) Eval-triggered alerting that fires to a webhook and shows in Console alerts tab, 4) Canary rollout to 2 pilot customers. Keep UI simple (no full policy editor). Thoughts?
Jia: Sounds right. Implementation risks: - quant smoke tests might be flaky across models (need strict eval fixtures), - automatic batching heuristics can regress tail latency for particular sequences unless we cap batch size per route. I propose a conservative default: batch_size cap + per-route override.
Owen: Agree. Add acceptance test: run synthetic customer replay for 72 hours on canary infra and compare token costs and quality metrics vs baseline. If regression window > 0.5% on quality, we don't flip.
Priya: Customers also asked for an audit log of when recommendations were applied + who applied them. That may be a blocker for some enterprise pilots.
Kai: Audit log is cheap on our side (emit event), but Console needs a small UI. We can do a minimal line-item in the activity feed for alpha.
Marta: Prioritization ask: which items are must-have for alpha vs alpha+? I'll propose must-have: recommendations engine (read-only), one-click apply with audit log, eval-alert webhook, canary gating. Alpha+ could include per-route override UI, richer telemetry, extra quant profiles.
Jia: Dev timeline: recommendation engine (2 sprints), one-click apply + rollback (1 sprint), eval-alert plumbing + webhook (1 sprint), infra + canary setup (1 sprint parallel). With overlap we can aim for a 6-week alpha if no big blockers.
Owen: Blockers to watch: model compatibility matrix for quant profiles, eval fixture coverage, and telemetry schema rollout coordination with partners.
Priya: I'll surface enterprise audit requirement to LibraryCo and Stripe and confirm whether audit feed + explainer doc suffices.
Marta: Action items: - Jia: draft tech spec for recommendation engine + conservative defaults by Tue. - Kai: telemetry schema change PR + canary checklist by Wed. - Owen: test plan for 72h replay + pass/fail thresholds by Wed. - Priya: customer confirm on audit requirement by Thu. I'll collate and push a short alpha acceptance doc by Friday.
Kai: deploy-bot: noted — will post canary infra checklist once PRs land. :robot_face:
deploy-bot: Canary checklist created: https://internal/redwood/canary-checks/optimize-alpha (placeholder) :white_check_mark:
Marta: Thanks team — scheduling 30m sync Thu to review tech spec + test plan. If anyone has hard objections to the must-have list speak now.
Jia: No objections from eng side.
Owen: No objections.
Priya: All good from CS, will update if customers push back.
